high.title: Peso May Test New Lows on Oil Price Surge
high.summary: The Philippine peso hit a fresh all-time low of PHP 61.847 per USD on Friday, deteriorating 9.7 centavos from Thursday's previous record of PHP 61.75. The intraday trough reached PHP 61.85, marking the weakest level the peso has ever traded. Year-to-date, the currency has now depreciated PHP 3.057 or approximately 4.94%, reflecting sustained and intensifying selling pressure. The primary driver is the escalating Iran conflict, which is pushing global oil prices sharply higher and rekindling domestic inflation fears — a particularly damaging combination for the Philippines given its heavy dependence on energy imports. For FX traders, the psychological PHP 62.00 level is now firmly in focus as a near-term test. A breach could accelerate stop-loss driven selling. BSP intervention risk is elevated at these levels, though the central bank's tolerance threshold remains unclear. Bond investors should brace for continued upward yield pressure, as a weaker peso complicates BSP's ability to ease policy. Watch for any BSP verbal or market intervention signals this week.

high.title: Government Securities Yields Jump on Inflation Fears
high.summary: Philippine government securities (GS) yields rose sharply across the curve last week, climbing an average of 19.98 basis points week-on-week, based on PHP Bloomberg Valuation Service Reference Rates as of July 24 published on the Philippine Dealing System. The twin catalysts were surging global oil prices — driven by the worsening Iran conflict — and the peso's slide to successive record lows, both of which are stoking domestic inflation expectations. Rising yields signal that bond investors are demanding higher risk premiums to hold Philippine government paper, reflecting fears that BSP may be forced to either pause its easing cycle or even reverse course if inflation materially re-accelerates. For fixed income portfolio managers, this is a critical inflection point: the nearly 20 bps average weekly move is unusually large and suggests the market is repricing the entire interest rate trajectory. Duration risk has increased materially. Watch the upcoming T-bill and T-bond auctions this week (see related article) for confirmation of whether demand holds or whether the government faces higher borrowing costs. Secondary market action in longer tenors will be key to monitor.

high.title: Debt Rates May End Mixed Amid Iran War and Oil Price Inflation Risks
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) faces a challenging auction week with PHP 50 billion in T-bills on offer Monday — split across 91-day (PHP 20B), 182-day (PHP 20B), and 364-day (PHP 10B) tenors — plus an additional PHP 50 billion in a dual-tenor T-bond auction on Tuesday. Market analysts expect rates to end mixed, with shorter-dated bills potentially finding support from risk-off liquidity demand, while longer tenors face upward rate pressure from inflation concerns linked to the Iran conflict and rising oil prices. No cash management bills will be offered this week. The auction results will serve as a critical real-time gauge of investor confidence in Philippine sovereign credit and the government's cost of financing. A significant uptick in awarded rates relative to secondary market benchmarks would confirm the bearish bond market sentiment already visible in last week's 19.98 bps average yield surge. For bond traders, the BTr's acceptance behavior — whether it rejects high bids or allows rates to rise — will signal the government's current tolerance for higher borrowing costs and provide directional cues for the broader GS curve.

high.title: Philippine Banking Industry Hopes Interest Rate Swaps Will Overtake FX Market
high.summary: The Bankers Association of the Philippines (BAP), through its Open Market Committee Chair Paul Raymond A. Favila (also Citi Philippines CEO), has signaled a structural ambition for the Philippine financial market: the interest rate swap (IRS) market could overtake the FX market in volume and activity — potentially as early as this year. This is a significant development for bond and FX traders alike. A more liquid and deep IRS market would allow banks and corporates to more efficiently hedge interest rate risk on peso-denominated liabilities, reducing over-reliance on FX instruments for risk management. For international fund managers, this signals a maturing fixed-income derivatives landscape in the Philippines, which could improve price discovery in government bond yields and reduce the cost of carry trades in PHP rates. A deeper IRS market would also give the BSP greater monetary policy transmission efficiency. **Watch:** Whether BSP regulatory frameworks support IRS market expansion and whether peso bond yield volatility decreases as IRS liquidity improves.

high.title: Philippine Banks' NPL Ratio Slips to 6-Month Low
high.summary: The Philippine banking sector's gross nonperforming loan (NPL) ratio improved to 3.29% in June — its lowest level in six months (last seen at 3.07% in December 2025) — down from 3.44% in May and 3.34% a year earlier, according to preliminary BSP data. The BSP attributed the improvement partly to easing inflation, which has made debt repayments more manageable for borrowers. For bond and equity investors, a declining NPL ratio is a constructive signal for banking sector credit quality, reducing tail risk on bank balance sheets and supporting PSEi financials. It also reinforces the case for continued BSP easing, as financial system stress is contained. For PHP traders, healthier bank fundamentals reduce the risk of systemic stress-driven capital outflows. **Watch:** Whether NPL ratios continue to decline in H2 2026 as the BSP's rate-cutting cycle filters through lending conditions, and whether provisioning requirements ease.

high.title: Philippine Peso Falls to Fresh Record Low vs US Dollar
high.summary:
The Philippine peso breached its previous all-time low, closing at **61.847 per USD** on Friday — surpassing the prior record of 61.75 set in late April. Intraday, the currency touched 61.85, marking a clear technical breakdown. The immediate catalyst was rising oil prices, which compound the Philippines' structural vulnerability as a net energy importer, worsening the trade and current account balance. The peso is now **one of Asia's worst-performing currencies in 2026, down approximately 5% year-to-date**. Markets are now eyeing **62.00 as the next key psychological and technical resistance level**, which, if breached, could trigger accelerated selling and force the BSP into more active FX intervention. For bond investors, a weaker peso raises imported inflation risks, potentially constraining the BSP's ability to cut rates. FX traders should watch for BSP verbal or direct intervention signals, oil price trajectory, and any shifts in USD sentiment driven by US data or Fed commentary. This is the most critical macro development of the week.

---

high.title: PSEi Falls on Profit Taking, Growing Gulf Tensions
high.summary:
The Philippine Stock Exchange index (PSEi) declined 1.27% or 81.92 points to close at 6,333.80, snapping a four-day winning streak, while the broader All Shares index slipped 0.32% to 3,439.58. The selloff was driven by profit-taking after the recent rally, but the more significant macro signal is the confluence of fresh inflation risks flagged in the article: **peso weakness** and **fuel price hikes** stemming from escalating Gulf tensions. For FX and bond traders, this is a critical combination — a weaker PHP feeding into imported inflation pressures, which could complicate the BSP's easing trajectory or prompt FX intervention. Rising oil prices due to Gulf instability represent an external supply shock that widens the Philippines' import bill, potentially widening the trade deficit and adding further downward pressure on the peso. Equity investors should monitor whether the PSEi support at the 6,300 level holds. Bond traders should watch for any inflation re-pricing in short-to-mid-tenor GS yields. The session opened at 6,461.34, suggesting significant intraday selling pressure — a bearish technical signal worth tracking in Wednesday's session.

---

medium.title: BSP Securities Rate Inches Up Amid Sustained Demand
medium.summary:
The average rate on BSP's 28-day short-term securities was nearly unchanged for a second consecutive week, suggesting the BSP's policy rate signaling remains stable despite broader market turbulence. Total bids reached PHP 62.179 billion against a PHP 40 billion offering — a healthy oversubscription ratio — though demand was softer than the prior week's PHP 70.69 billion in tenders. The continued strong oversubscription indicates ample domestic liquidity conditions and ongoing appetite for BSP paper as a safe short-term parking facility. For rates traders, the relative stability of BSP bill rates — even as secondary market GS yields surged nearly 20 bps last week — suggests a widening divergence between the BSP's controlled short end and market-driven longer tenors. This dynamic warrants close monitoring: if inflation risks materialize further, pressure on the BSP to adjust its policy stance could intensify, potentially ending the era of stable BSP bill rates.

---

medium.title: Philippine Exports Worth $6.25 Billion Exposed to 12.5% US Tariff — DTI
medium.summary:
The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) has assessed that approximately $6.25 billion worth of Philippine exports — representing 34.28% of total Philippine exports to the US based on 2025 trade data — face exposure to the new US 12.5% import tariff. This is a meaningful trade risk for the Philippines' current account dynamics, as export revenue compression could widen the trade deficit and exert depreciation pressure on the PHP over the medium term. Reduced export competitiveness may also dampen FDI inflows into export-oriented manufacturing sectors. For peso traders, this adds a structural headwind to the PHP/USD outlook and should be monitored alongside BSP intervention activity. **Watch:** Negotiations between Philippine and US trade officials, and whether export diversion to other markets can offset lost US-bound revenue.

---

medium.title: Worsening Iran Conflict to Weigh on Philippine Shares
medium.summary: The PSEi closed at **6,281.01 on Friday**, down marginally by 0.03%, capping a weekly decline of **123.1 points from 6,404.11**. Analysts flag escalating geopolitical tensions linked to the Iran conflict as a key headwind, alongside inflation risks — both of which are likely amplifying peso weakness and dampening investor risk appetite. President Marcos Jr.'s State of the Nation Address is also in focus as a potential policy catalyst. For equity investors, sustained geopolitical uncertainty and a depreciating peso create a challenging environment; foreign fund outflows remain a risk. Watch for any fiscal or investment policy signals from SONA that could provide near-term direction.

medium.title: Shares Sink to 6,200 Range as Peso Revisits Record Low
medium.summary: The PSEi dropped **1.04% (65.95 points) to 6,267.85** on Wednesday, its second consecutive session of losses, as the peso's return to record-low territory triggered broad risk-off sentiment and profit-taking. The correlation between peso weakness and equity market underperformance is clearly evident this week, reflecting foreign investor caution and reduced risk appetite. The index opening at 6,334.88 before closing sharply lower suggests intraday selling pressure was significant. This session, combined with the peso's subsequent fresh record low on July 24, underscores the negative feedback loop between currency depreciation and equity outflows that fund managers should monitor closely.

medium.title: Stocks Inch Higher on Bargain Hunting After Slump
medium.summary: The PSEi recovered modestly on Thursday, gaining **0.24% (15.27 points) to close at 6,283.12**, as bargain hunters stepped in following two consecutive sessions of losses. The rebound was tepid and driven by selective dip-buying rather than any fundamental shift in sentiment, with geopolitical concerns continuing to linger. The limited upside on the recovery day — followed by another near-flat close on Friday — suggests the market lacks conviction to stage a meaningful rally in the current environment of peso weakness and global uncertainty.
